lean_implies_source.reasoning: The target gives, for every real p>=1, the standard-normal Lp norm as the exact Gamma expression. D010 identifies the norm with the p-th absolute moment to power 1/p. Positivity and real-power laws rewrite the target's (2^(p/2)*ratio)^(1/p) as sqrt(2)*ratio^(1/p). The same exact formula, together with the standard Gamma/Stirling asymptotic, yields the source's explicitly requested O(sqrt(p)) deduction.

Applying it to the canonical identity random variable under gaussianReal 0 1, interpreting its Lp norm via eLpNorm', and regrouping the positive real powers yields precisely the Lean equality.

rationale: The Lean proposition is a faithful equivalent presentation of Exercise 2.5.1. It fixes the standard Gaussian as the identity map under its canonical law, and eLpNorm' is definitionally the required absolute-moment norm. Its Gamma expression is algebraically the source expression on p>=1. Although the source also displays the O(sqrt(p)) corollary, the target's exact identity for every p>=1 entails that corollary; conversely, the source's exact identity specializes to and algebraically yields the target. All 46 semantic dependencies are accounted for and introduce no hidden restriction, vacuity, or mismatch.
